themes.title: OpenAI pushes global AI safety standards ahead of UN week
themes.summary: OpenAI published a proposal for international AI safety coordination and joined calls for US-led global standards, with Sam Altman set to brief the UN Security Council this week. Treasury Secretary Bessent confirmed Washington and Beijing discussed an AI safety system ahead of the Trump-Xi summit. The direction of travel: safety standardisation is being negotiated as trade diplomacy, not just lab policy.
themes.angle: Safety standards are becoming the new trade lanes - watch which bloc GCC supply chains must comply with.

themes.title: Meta's Muse tops app charts and reignites the AI rally
themes.summary: Meta's consumer agent Muse hit the top of app-store charts and dragged global AI and chip stocks back up after a rough stretch driven by calls to slow AI development. The Information reports Amazon is blocking Muse and OpenAI is building counter-features against Grok Bot while weighing a response. The market read: consumer agent adoption is now the marginal signal for chip demand and capex confidence.
themes.angle: Agent adoption, not model releases, is what moved the tape today.

themes.title: AI power crunch and the new capital stack
themes.summary: Google agreed to fund around 96MW of new nuclear capacity at two Georgia plants as the FT pegs the US data-centre power gap at 'six New Yorks'. SoftBank's $50bn data-centre group slowed its IPO on AI-slowdown fears, even as SoftBank launched one of the biggest junk-bond deals on record (target over $11bn) to fund its OpenAI bet. Governments are responding: a US congressman wants a national data-centre strategy, an Australian state bans data centres from residential areas, and the WEF flags a $1tn unlock opportunity in the ~$7tn global buildout.
themes.angle: The AI buildout now runs on nuclear megawatts and junk-bond markets.

themes.title: British Columbia sues OpenAI over mass-shooting warning failure
themes.summary: Canada's British Columbia filed suit in California arguing ChatGPT logs should have alerted police after an account linked to a mass shooting in the province was flagged. Whatever its merits, the case pushes AI liability from speculative to concrete: providers are now accountable for what they could have inferred from their own systems.
themes.angle: The first big test of 'failure to warn' liability for a frontier lab.

themes.title: UAE: agentic AI enters public services; cyber and quantum push
themes.summary: The UAE government partnered with Dell to advance agentic AI in public services, and Meta joined the UAE Cyber Security Council to launch Wearables Studio UAE, the nation's first AI-wearables talent programme. TII's Abu Dhabi Quantum Optical Ground Station pushes secure communications into space, while CrowdStrike warns AI agents are creating a new cyber battleground for GCC organisations.
themes.angle: Abu Dhabi pairs agentic-AI adoption with a quantum-hardened security posture.

themes.title: Frontier ecosystem: Grok on Bedrock, stress tests, agent memory
themes.summary: xAI's Grok 4.6 landed on Amazon Bedrock, widening enterprise distribution; The Information reports OpenAI and Anthropic nearly signed a deal to stress-test each other's models. OpenAI also shipped a maths advisory group, a GPT-6 Astra customer story and V7 agent-memory tooling, while Luma's CEO argues world models need more intelligence. The coupling of models and agents for enterprise work is accelerating.
themes.angle: The frontier is distributing: model access is becoming a procurement decision.
